name: Long Beach International Airport
before:
A small Los Angeles alternative, three miles from downtown Long Beach and about twenty miles from LAX. For clients staying in Long Beach or northern Orange County it is far quicker than the main airport, and considerably calmer.

The trade off is choice. JetBlue ran an operating base here until October 2020, when it moved to LAX, and Southwest is now the largest carrier. Traffic sits around 1.4 million boardings a year, which makes it the tenth busiest airport in California.

It is hemmed in by housing, and that shapes how it works. Long Beach operates one of the strictest airport noise ordinances in the United States, so do not assume a late arrival or departure is possible without checking.

The field is also called Daugherty Field, after the local aviator Earl Daugherty, and carries a mix of commercial, cargo, military and general aviation traffic.
after:
A small Los Angeles alternative, a few miles from downtown Long Beach. It sits between Los Angeles and Orange counties, which suits clients staying in Long Beach or northern Orange County, and it is known for an easygoing atmosphere.

The trade off is choice. JetBlue, once the biggest airline here, has gone. Southwest is now by far the largest carrier. Traffic was about 3.8 million passengers in 2025, and it ranks tenth in California for boardings.

It is hemmed in by housing, and that shapes how it works. Long Beach operates one of the strictest airport noise ordinances in the United States, so do not assume a late arrival or departure is possible without checking.

The field is also called Daugherty Field after the local aviator Earl Daugherty. It carries a mix of commercial, cargo and general aviation traffic.
